claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.3, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.26 to 2.23 (change -0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.26 to 0.49. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.23 (as submitted, 8 bps: 2.26); it breaks even at 188.5 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.26 against 2.26 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.01 against 2.26 in research, a gap of +2.27.
The best year gives 17% of total P&L (year 4) and calm regimes give 91%; Sharpe is 2.56 in calm and 1.07 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.09, so the claimed 2.30 becomes 2.21 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.36 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.01, 95th percentile 0.53).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 24% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 18% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
